title: Metrics Bridge: aggregation gateway for low-cardinality inference KPIs
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
Build a lightweight aggregation gateway ("metrics-bridge") that sits between the inference runtime's OTLP exporter and our long-term Prometheus/TSDB pipeline. The bridge will: (1) convert high-cardinality OTel metrics into a set of production-friendly Prometheus metrics and histograms; (2) compute and export Redwood-specific inference KPIs (per-model token latency percentiles, batch efficiency, KV cache hit-rate, request failure ratios) at configurable aggregation windows; (3) expose both Prometheus remote_write-compatible endpoints and OTLP-compatible endpoints for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Motivation:
Current raw OTLP ingestion overwhelms the Prometheus ingestion path due to high cardinality (model_id, model_version, user_route, prompt_tag, adapter_id, batch_size). Producing stable, low-cardinality KPIs with correct percentiles and error budgets is critical for Console dashboards, SLOs, and automated rollouts. Existing work (ENG-16320, ENG-23377) addressed metric sharding and SLI computation, but we need an aggregation layer focused on inference semantics and deployment portability (hosted + dedicated + private).

Goals and success criteria:
- Deliver a stateless, horizontally scalable service that reduces metric cardinality by 90% for KPI streams while preserving signal for latency/error SLOs.
- Provide consistent p50/p95/p99 token-latency histograms per model/model_family and per-route, exported every 30s and 5m windows.
- Compute derived KPIs: batch_efficiency = tokens_per_gpu_call / theoretical_peak; kv_cache_hit_rate = hits / (hits+misses), and request_error_rate with error bucketing.
- Support feature flags to enable/disable specific aggregations per-customer for Dedicated/Private.
- Expose both Prometheus remote_write and OTLP exporter outputs so downstream consumers (Grafana, Bigtable/TSDB, Alertmanager) can use either path.

Design notes:
- Ingestion: accept OTLP metrics + JSON-encoded meta labels from the runtime sidecar. Provide an optional lightweight sidecar mode for private infra where running an extra process is preferable to opening new network routes.
- Cardinality reduction: primary strategy is label normalization + dynamic roll-ups (map model_version -> model_family, drop ephemeral labels like request_id unless flagged) and controlled top-k dimensioning with 'other' buckets.
- Percentile estimates: use HDR histograms with bounded memory per key and configurable decay windows. For short SLO windows (30s) use reservoir+extrapolation to reduce error on sparse keys.
- Sampling: deterministic sampling for high-volume clients (token-level sampling with deterministic hashing on trace_id) to maintain reproducible KPIs and enable attribution.
- Trace correlation: add standardized span attributes (redwood.model_id, redwood.model_version, redwood.route, redwood.batch_size, redwood.kv_cache_hit) so traces can be stitched to computed KPIs. The bridge will forward correlation IDs to the tracing backends for ad-hoc investigation.
- Output schemas: define Prometheus metric naming conventions: redwood_inference_token_latency_seconds{model_family,route,window="30s",quantile="0.95"}, redwood_inference_kv_cache_hit_ratio{model_family,route}, redwood_inference_batch_efficiency_ratio. Documented in CONFLUENCE: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Metrics+Bridge+Schema

Operational considerations:
- Autoscaling: horizontal pods with CPU-bound aggregation; use partitioning by model_family for sharding to reduce cross-node memory.
- Backpressure: when bridge is under load, it should drop non-essential labels and fall back to coarse buckets; emit a health metric about dropped_labels_count for alerting.
- Persistence: keep ephemeral HDR state in-memory; support optional write-through diagnostics into a short-lived TSDB for debugging.
- Security: support mTLS between runtime sidecars and bridge; per-tenant ACLs for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype: implement a minimal Go service that ingests OTLP metrics and exports p50/p95 histograms to a Prometheus remote_write test cluster. (2 weeks).
2) Internal dogfood: route 5% of hosted traffic to bridge path, compare KPI deltas against baseline (ENG-21901 style downsampled export). (3 weeks).
3) Add sidecar mode and determinisitic sampling, prepare Dedicated deployment packaging. (2 weeks).
4) Canary: enable for a small Dedicated customer with SRE/PM supervision, iterate. (2 weeks).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Estimation error for percentiles on sparse keys; mitigated via reservoir+HDR and merging strategies but will not be exact.
- Increased operational complexity: one more component to manage in Dedicated/Private. Mitigate with sidecar option and clear runbooks.
- Possible customer confusion between raw OTLP metrics and bridged KPIs; document differences and provide both streams for a transition period.

Deliverables:
- metrics-bridge service code, Helm chart, sidecar image, and integration tests.
- Prometheus/Grafana dashboard templates for token latency, kv cache, batch efficiency.
- Migration guide and Confluence spec.
- Canaried rollout and post-mortem with stability metrics.
